lineage_note: Top tier of English football. 1888-89 to 1891-92 = Football League (single division); 1892-93 to 1991-92 = Football League First Division; 1992-93 on = Premier League.
player_of_season_award: FWA Footballer of the Year (Football Writers' Association), 1947-48 to 2025-26 - one award for the whole run; it is England-wide but every winner except Dave Mackay (shared 1968-69) played in the top tier.
sources: Wikipedia season articles 1889-90, 1895-96, 1905-06, 1937-38 Football League (disputed top-scorer counts)

seasons.notes: Preston North End unbeaten and also won the FA Cup (the first Double).
Top scorer goals disputed: RSSSF and the Wikipedia season article give Jimmy Ross 24; the Wikipedia top-scorers list gives 22. 24 used (two sources).
Top scorers: Wikipedia list and RSSSF give 20 each for Bloomer and Campbell (other sources give 22 or 24); 20 used.
Top scorer: RSSSF, footballsite and the Wikipedia season article give Walter White (Bolton) 26; the Wikipedia top-scorers list credits Albert Shepherd (Bolton). White used.
Top scorer goals disputed (28/34/38 across sources); 28 used (footballsite + Wikipedia season article).
League suspended: Second World War (1939-40 abandoned after three matches).
FWA award shared: Tony Book (Manchester City) and Dave Mackay (Derby County, then Second Division).
Ian Wright: 5 goals for Crystal Palace, 24 for Arsenal.
Teddy Sheringham: 1 goal for Nottingham Forest, 21 for Tottenham Hotspur. Eric Cantona: assists for Leeds United and Manchester United combined (16).
